status: prototype preview, not shipped and not registered in PNG_UNIT_SPRITES
generator: ChatGPT image generation (project owner, paid plan)
prompt_note: prompt.txt is the second prompt the assistant wrote (a rewrite of the first that asks for an 8-frame walk and clearer damage tiers). ChatGPT would not run it as written and altered it; the prompt it actually used was not available when this record was written, and the owner has said they will supply it as a template.
licence_note: Covered by the project's non-commercial posture (docs/asset-rights-ledger.md). If this art is adopted for the game it needs a ledger family row and a provenance record under design/png-sprites/sources/ like the other generated units.
originals_note: The seven downloaded originals (about 11 MB) are not committed. Only the re-encoded sheet.png and mask.png are, built by scripts/sprite-puppet/strips.py from decoded pixels (no EXIF/XMP/ICC or C2PA survives).
scan: python3 -I scripts/portrait-pixelate/portrait_pixelate.py scan: all seven passed (PNG magic bytes, nothing after the image stream, one frame, within the pixel limit). ClamAV was not installed, so only the structural checks ran.
layout_note: This set came back as RGBA with a real transparent background (no magenta), with the frames of each animation laid out in a grid rather than one row. The hit and defeat images carry a faint glow at alpha 20 or below, which the tool discards.

originals.role: walk, 8 frames (4 x 2 grid), the fourth walk attempt

walk_attempts.note: The walk was redrawn three times. prompt-walk.txt is the prompt for the last one (a relaxed, low-foot walk); the earlier ones were rejected: the second set's walk repeated one step so one leg always led, and the third had high knees and uneven pacing.

superseded_first_set.note: The first run (single-row strips on a magenta field) was replaced by the set above. Its sheet is in the git history of this branch.
